q: Which of the following punishments can be awarded by the Lok Sabha to a member held guilty of breach of privileges or contempt of the House?
options: Expulsion from the House and thereby declaring his seat as vacant
key_text: Expulsion from the House and thereby declaring his seat as vacant
explanation: A House punishes members and outsiders by reprimand, admonition or imprisonment, and members also by suspension or expulsion (Raja Ram Pal 2007 upheld expulsion). It does not impose fines, and imprisonment lasts only till the session ends, so 'six months' is wrong.

notes.text: - **Punishments:** **reprimand, admonition, imprisonment** (only till the session ends), and for members **suspension or expulsion** (seat declared vacant). **No fine**; "six months' imprisonment" ✗.

q: Which of the following punishments can the Lok Sabha impose on members who behave in breach of privilege or contempt of the House?
options: Expelling from the House and declaring the seat vacant
key_text: Expelling from the House and declaring the seat vacant
explanation: A House punishes by reprimand, admonition or imprisonment, and members also by suspension or expulsion. It does not impose fines, and imprisonment cannot outlast the session, so expulsion with the seat declared vacant is the valid option.

notes.text: - **Punishments:** **reprimand, admonition, imprisonment** (only till the session ends), and for members **suspension or expulsion** (seat declared vacant). **No fine**; "six months' imprisonment" ✗.

q: Which of the following statement is correct regarding Parliamentary Privileges?
options: Parliamentary Privileges are the privileges tha are enjoyed collectively by each House of the Parliament, and not by the Members individually
Only Members can be punished for contempt by reprimand and admonition but not outsiders
The phrase 'Breach of Privilege' has wider implications than the 'Contempt of the House
The Members cannot be arrested during the session of Parliament but this privilege is available only in civil cases and not in criminal cases or preventive detention cases
key_text: The Members cannot be arrested during the session of Parliament but this privilege is available only in civil cases and not in criminal cases or preventive detention cases
explanation: Members cannot be arrested during a session and 40 days before and after it, but only in civil cases, not criminal or preventive detention cases. Privileges are both collective and individual, outsiders can be punished too, and contempt is wider than breach of privilege.

notes.text: - **Contempt is wider** than breach: every breach is contempt, but not every contempt (e.g. disobeying a House order) is a breach of a specific privilege.
- "Privileges are only collective" ✗ / "only individual" ✗ – they are **both**.

q: All following statements regarding the privileges of Parliament members are correct except
explanation: Members' individual privileges include freedom of speech, freedom from arrest in civil cases and freedom from attendance as a witness while the House sits. Privileges are also collective (of each House), so 'only individual freedom' is the incorrect statement.

notes.text: - "Privileges are only collective" ✗ / "only individual" ✗ – they are **both**.

q: Which of the following is true according to the Constitution of India?
options: The Prime Minister is the leader of the majority party
The president appoints the Prime Minister

q: India is following Parliamentary form of government. In this regard all statements given below are correct, except
options: The collective responsibility is to the house of the people even though some of the ministers may be the members of the Council of the States
The President of India is the real head of the executive
Ministers shall be individually responsible to the President and shall be liable to dismissal even when they may have the confidence ofthe Legislature
In a parliamentary form of government, the tenure of office of the council of ministers is dependent on the will of the legislature
key_text: The President of India is the real head of the executive
explanation: The President is only the nominal (de jure) head; the real executive is the PM and Council of Ministers. The other statements correctly describe collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha, ministers holding office at the President's pleasure and tenure depending on the legislature.

notes.text: - **⚠ Traps:** collective responsibility to "Parliament" is accepted only when the Lok Sabha is not offered; "Council of Ministers responsible to both Houses" ✗ (UPSC 2007 A false, R true – members of both Houses can be ministers); "Cabinet headed by the Head of State" ✗ (UPSC 2013: 1 and 2 only); "President is the real head of the executive" ✗ (APPSC G2).

q: As per the Constitution, the Council of Union Ministers is collectively responsible to
explanation: Under Art. 75(3) the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, not to both Houses, the President or the ruling party.

q: A parliamentary executive means?

An officer working in the Parliament

notes.text: - **Parliamentary executive** = an executive **dependent on the support of a majority in Parliament** – not "elected by Parliament", not "Parliament acting as executive".

q: In a parliamentary government, the executive is responsible to the
explanation: In a parliamentary government the executive (Council of Ministers) is responsible to the legislature, in India to the Lok Sabha.

notes.text: - **Main principle:** **responsibility of the executive to the legislature**; the legislature controls the executive. "Legislature and Executive are independent" is the **presidential** feature.

q:
Two statements are given below, one labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other labelled as
Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In a parliamentary form of government it is not the lower house which controls the executive but the executive which controls the house.
Reason (R): The Council of Ministers is constituted from within the legislature.
Choose the correct answer from among the codes given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
key_text: A is false, but R is true
explanation: In the parliamentary form the executive is collectively responsible to and controlled by the lower house (Art. 75(3)), so A as a statement of the system is false; R is true – the Council of Ministers is drawn from the legislature.

notes.text: - **Defining test:** India is parliamentary because the **Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha** (Art. 75(3); States Art. 164(2)) – not because the Lok Sabha is directly elected, Parliament can amend the Constitution or the Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved (UPSC 2015).

- **⚠ Traps:** collective responsibility to "Parliament" is accepted only when the Lok Sabha is not offered; "Council of Ministers responsible to both Houses" ✗ (UPSC 2007 A false, R true – members of both Houses can be ministers); "Cabinet headed by the Head of State" ✗ (UPSC 2013: 1 and 2 only); "President is the real head of the executive" ✗ (APPSC G2).

q: Which of the following statements are correct about Presidential system? i. President is head of the State. ii. President is head of the Government. iii. President is directly elected by the people. iv. President is accountable to legislature.

explanation: A Governor holds office for five years (Art. 156), subject to the President's pleasure.

q: The Governor of a State in India is responsible to the
explanation: The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President (Art. 156(1)) and is thus answerable to him, not to the State Legislature or Council of Ministers.

q: The Governor is impeached through
explanation: The Constitution provides no impeachment for a Governor; he holds office during the pleasure of the President (Art. 156). Only the President is impeached (Art. 61).

explanation: A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly except on the recommendation of the Governor (Art. 207) – not the CM, Finance Minister or Speaker.

q: Who constitutes the State Finance Commission?
explanation: Art. 243I: the Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission every five years to review Panchayat finances – not the CM, the State Legislature or the RBI.

q: Who of the following sends fortnightly reports to the President of India about the functioning of a State Government?
options: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
The Chief Secretary of the State
explanation: By convention the Governor, as the Centre's representative, sends fortnightly reports to the President on the State's affairs – not the CM, Speaker or Chief Secretary.

exam: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer, Royalty Inspector 2020
q: Who inaugurates the state legislature and the first session of each year, by addressing the Assembly, outlining the new administrative policies of the ruling government?
explanation: Under Art. 176 the Governor addresses the Legislature at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year, outlining the government's policies.

q: Who of the following is empowered to dissolve the Legislative Assembly of a State?
explanation: Under Art. 174(2)(b) the Governor dissolves the Legislative Assembly, normally on the advice of the CM – the Speaker, CM or Chief Justice cannot dissolve it.

notes.text: - So the Telugu State had been under President's Rule **twice as of 2004** (1954-55 and 1973). The **1984 Nadendla** episode was **not** President's Rule.

q: The orders passed by the Governor of a State (Article 163) of a State fall in four categories. Find out the category which is not subject to Judicial Review.
options: The exercise of executive power in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution by or under the order of the Governor
Orders passed by the Governor on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister
Where the Governor acts without the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers and acts in his own discretion
key_text: Where the Governor acts without the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers and acts in his own discretion
explanation: Where the Governor acts in his own discretion without aid and advice, Art. 163(2) makes his decision final, so it is not open to judicial review; executive action, orders on advice and pardon orders are reviewable.

notes.text: - Of four categories of the Governor's orders (executive action, orders on aid and advice, pardon, discretion), the one **not subject to judicial review** is where he **acts in his own discretion** without aid and advice.

q: The orders passed by the Governor of a State (Article 163) fall in four categories. Find out the category which is NOT subject to Judicial Review.
options: Where the Governor acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers
Where the Governor acts without the aid and advice of the Council of his own discretion
Where the Governor enters and acts in legislative matters
Where the Governor addresses the legislature

q: The President may appoint a Governor of a State as the administrator of an adjoining Union Territory. Such Governor in the administration of the Union Territory shall exercise his functions
options: With the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers of the State
As such administrator independently of his Council of Ministers
Under the direct supervision of the President
With the help of a council appointed by the Union Territory
key_text: As such administrator independently of his Council of Ministers
explanation: Under Art. 239(2), a Governor appointed administrator of an adjoining UT acts as such independently of his State Council of Ministers.

q: What is "Composite floor test" in case of voting in a State Assembly?
options: Voting in the Assembly as directed by the Speaker when there is more than one person staking claim to form government and majority is not clear.
Voting in the Assembly as directed by the Governor when there is more than one person staking claim to form Government and majority is not clear.
Voting in the Assembly to approve different bills at one time.
Voting in the Assembly where in Legislators from Government and opposition sit in a mingled fashion and vote in pairs.
key_text: Voting in the Assembly as directed by the Governor when there is more than one person staking claim to form Government and majority is not clear.
explanation: A composite floor test is held when more than one person stakes claim to form the government and the majority is unclear; the Governor calls the Assembly to decide by vote who has the majority (as in Jagdambika Pal, 1998).

exam: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer Paper-III (Indian Con
q: Mark the incorrect option with respect to the President's rule in an Indian state.
options: The President's rule is imposed under powers conferred by Article 356 of the Constitution
Article 355 imposes a duty upon the Centre to ensure that all state governments in India function under the provisions given in the Constitution
The state will be administered by the Governor on behalf of the President.
The central cabinet passes the state bills and budget when the legislative assembly is suspended or dissolved under the President's rule.
key_text: The central cabinet passes the state bills and budget when the legislative assembly is suspended or dissolved under the President's rule.
explanation: Incorrect: under President's Rule Parliament (Art. 357), not the Union Cabinet, passes the State's Bills and budget. Art. 356 is the power, Art. 355 the Centre's duty, and the Governor administers the State for the President.

notes.text: - Effects: the President takes over the State executive, administered by the **Governor on his behalf**; the Legislature's powers go to **Parliament** (**Art. 357**) – **Parliament**, not the Union Cabinet, passes State Bills and budget; the Assembly is **suspended or dissolved** (not automatically dissolved); **Art. 19 is not suspended**; the High Court is untouched.

q: President's Rule was imposed recently in the State of Manipur under which Article of the Constitution ?
explanation: President's Rule is imposed under Art. 356; Manipur's latest spell began on 13 Feb 2025 (revoked Feb 2026). Art. 352 is National Emergency.

notes.text: - Imposed when the government of a State **cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution** – on the **Governor's report** or **otherwise** (suo motu).

q: If the State fail to carry out directives of the Union Government, the President canto
options: Send reserve police to the State
Impose president rule on the State
Direct the Governor to dismiss the State council of ministers
key_text: Impose president rule on the State
explanation: If a State fails to comply with Union directions, Art. 365 lets the President hold that its government cannot be carried on per the Constitution and impose President's Rule (Art. 356).

notes.text: - Second ground: **Art. 365** – a State **fails to comply with Union directions** (Art. 355 = Centre's duty to ensure States run per the Constitution).
